questions.q: What is the capital city of Senegal?
questions.e: Dakar is the capital of Senegal.

questions.q: Which ocean lies west of Senegal?
questions.e: Senegal has a coastline on the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.q: Which language is the official language of Senegal?
questions.e: French is Senegal’s official language; many national languages are also spoken.

questions.q: Gorée Island is located near which city?
questions.e: Gorée Island lies close to Dakar.

questions.q: Which large river forms part of Senegal’s northern border?
questions.e: The Senegal River runs along part of the border with Mauritania.

questions.q: Which Senegalese national park is known for wildlife and lies in the southeast?
questions.e: Niokolo-Koba is a major national park in southeastern Senegal.

questions.q: Which country is directly south of Senegal and is surrounded by Senegal on most sides?
questions.e: The Gambia follows the Gambia River and is surrounded by Senegal except for its Atlantic coast.

questions.q: What is the name of the westernmost point of mainland Africa, near Dakar?
questions.e: Pointe des Almadies is near Dakar on the western edge of mainland Africa.

questions.q: Which Senegalese region is especially known for its mangroves and river delta?
questions.e: The Sine-Saloum area includes an important delta and mangrove ecosystem.

questions.q: What is a baobab?
questions.e: The baobab is a large tree found in Africa.

questions.q: Which country is famous for the ancient city of Timbuktu?
questions.e: Timbuktu is a historic city in Mali.

questions.q: Which African country has the city of Mombasa on its Indian Ocean coast?
questions.e: Mombasa is a coastal city in Kenya.

questions.q: Mount Kilimanjaro is in which country?
questions.e: Mount Kilimanjaro is in northeastern Tanzania.

questions.q: Which waterfall lies on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe?
questions.e: Victoria Falls is on the Zambezi River at the Zambia–Zimbabwe border.

questions.q: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.e: The Sahara is the world’s largest hot desert.

questions.q: What is the capital of Kenya?
questions.e: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya.

questions.q: Which sea separates northeastern Africa from the Arabian Peninsula?
questions.e: The Red Sea lies between northeastern Africa and the Arabian Peninsula.

questions.q: Which country became independent from Britain in 1957 and was formerly called the Gold Coast?
questions.e: The former Gold Coast became independent Ghana in 1957.

questions.q: Lake Victoria borders Kenya, Uganda and which other country?
questions.e: Lake Victoria is shared by Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya.

questions.q: Which African country is home to the ancient rock-hewn churches of Lalibela?
questions.e: Lalibela’s rock-hewn churches are in Ethiopia.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a national park?
questions.e: National parks help conserve habitats and wildlife.

questions.q: Which animal is the largest land mammal in Africa?
questions.e: The African elephant is the largest land mammal on land.

questions.q: Which continent is directly north of Senegal across the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.e: Europe lies north of Africa across the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.q: Which river flows through Egypt and empties into the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.e: The Nile flows north through Egypt to the Mediterranean.

questions.q: Which Senegalese dish was added to UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2021?
questions.e: UNESCO lists Ceebu Jën as a culinary art of Senegal.

questions.q: Xooy is a divination ceremony associated with which Senegalese community?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Xooy as a Serer divination ceremony.

questions.q: Kankurang is described by UNESCO as which kind of heritage?
questions.e: UNESCO lists Kankurang as a Manding initiatory rite.

questions.q: The Stone Circles of Senegambia are shared by Senegal and which country?
questions.e: The UNESCO site includes components in Senegal and The Gambia.

questions.q: Which two named stone-circle groups are in Senegal?
questions.e: UNESCO locates Wanar and Sine Ngayène in Senegal.

questions.q: Which two named stone-circle groups are in The Gambia?
questions.e: UNESCO locates Wassu and Kerbatch in The Gambia.

questions.q: What are many of the mounds associated with the Senegambian stone circles?
questions.e: UNESCO describes associated tumuli as burial mounds.

questions.q: Which three peoples are named in the Bassari Country World Heritage site?
questions.e: The UNESCO site's name identifies the Bassari, Fula and Bedik landscapes.

questions.q: In which part of Senegal is Bassari Country located?
questions.e: UNESCO locates Bassari Country in south-eastern Senegal.

questions.q: What is a feature of the Bassari landscape described by UNESCO?
questions.e: UNESCO describes terraces and rice paddies among Bassari villages.

questions.q: What is characteristic of many Bedik village houses?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Bedik villages with huts and steep thatched roofs.

questions.q: What is the Saloum Delta especially known for in its cultural landscape?
questions.e: UNESCO highlights shell mounds and coastal livelihoods in the delta.

questions.q: What kind of water is found in parts of the Saloum Delta?
o: Water with no salt at all
questions.e: UNESCO describes the delta's water as brackish.

questions.q: What traditional activities helped shape the Saloum Delta landscape?
questions.e: UNESCO describes shellfish gathering and fishing practices.

questions.q: Where is the Island of Saint-Louis situated?
o: At the source of the Nile
In the middle of Lake Victoria
At the mouth of the Senegal River
On the coast of The Gambia River
questions.e: UNESCO places Saint-Louis at the mouth of the Senegal River.

questions.q: Which city became Senegal’s capital after the role moved from Saint-Louis?
questions.e: Dakar is Senegal's national capital.

questions.q: Which Senegalese island was inscribed on the World Heritage List in 1978?
questions.e: UNESCO lists Gorée as inscribed in 1978.

questions.q: In which year was the Island of Saint-Louis inscribed on UNESCO’s World Heritage List?
questions.e: UNESCO records the Island of Saint-Louis inscription in 2000.

questions.q: In which year was the Saloum Delta inscribed on the World Heritage List?
questions.e: UNESCO records the Saloum Delta inscription in 2011.

questions.q: In which year were the Stone Circles of Senegambia inscribed?
questions.e: UNESCO records the inscription in 2006.

questions.q: Which Senegalese World Heritage site is known for a bird sanctuary?
questions.e: Djoudj is listed by UNESCO as a national bird sanctuary.

questions.q: What kind of heritage is Ceebu Jën recognized as?
questions.e: UNESCO lists Ceebu Jën as a culinary art.

questions.q: What do UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscapes often show?
o: Only the weather of a place
How people and their environment interact
questions.e: Cultural landscapes reflect relationships between communities and their environment.

questions.q: What is a tumulus in the context of the Senegambian stone circles?
o: A mound associated with a burial
questions.e: UNESCO describes tumuli as burial mounds.

questions.q: Near which Ghanaian city are the Asante Traditional Buildings located?
questions.e: UNESCO locates the buildings near Kumasi.

questions.q: Which materials are named for the Asante Traditional Buildings?
questions.e: UNESCO lists earth, wood and straw.

questions.q: What decorative feature appears on Asante building walls?
questions.e: UNESCO notes decorative bas-reliefs.

questions.q: In which country are the Royal Palaces of Abomey?
questions.e: Abomey is in Benin.

questions.q: How many kings succeeded one another in Abomey between 1625 and 1900?
questions.e: UNESCO counts twelve successive kings.

questions.q: What material formed the traditional walls around Abomey palace compounds?
questions.e: UNESCO describes walls made of cob.

questions.q: Lamu Old Town is on the coast of which country?
questions.e: Lamu is on Kenya’s East African coast.

questions.q: Which historic culture is especially represented by Lamu Old Town?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Lamu as a Swahili settlement.

questions.q: Which pair of materials was used in historic buildings in Lamu?
questions.e: UNESCO names coral stone and mangrove timber.

questions.q: Great Zimbabwe is located in which country?
questions.e: The monument is in Zimbabwe.

questions.q: Which people are associated with the founding of Great Zimbabwe?
questions.e: UNESCO identifies the builders as the Shona.

questions.q: Aksum is an ancient site in which country?
questions.e: Aksum is in northern Ethiopia.

questions.q: Stone Town is a historic settlement in which country?
questions.e: Stone Town is on Zanzibar, part of Tanzania.

questions.q: Which coastal culture is represented by Stone Town?
questions.e: UNESCO describes it as a Swahili coastal trading town.

questions.q: Which materials are named in the construction of Stone Town buildings?
questions.e: UNESCO names coral stone and mangrove timber.

questions.q: Which set of cultural influences is reflected in Stone Town?
questions.e: UNESCO describes these influences in the town’s architecture.

questions.q: Timbuktu is in which West African country?
questions.e: Timbuktu is a historic city in Mali.

questions.q: What was Sankore in Timbuktu?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Sankore as a university and learning centre.

questions.q: Which goods were traded in Timbuktu’s historic markets?
questions.e: UNESCO notes manuscript, salt and gold trade.

questions.q: Which mosque is one of Timbuktu’s three historic great mosques?
questions.e: Sankore is one of the three mosques listed by UNESCO.

questions.q: The Old Towns of Djenné are in which country?
questions.e: Djenné is in Mali.

questions.q: Which building material is especially important in Djenné’s historic architecture?
questions.e: UNESCO highlights the use of earth in its architecture.

questions.q: Why were many traditional houses in Djenné built on raised mounds?
o: To be closer to the sea
To reduce the effect of seasonal floods
questions.e: UNESCO notes that the mounds protect houses from seasonal floods.

questions.q: Which historic trade helped Djenné grow as a market centre?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Djenné as an important link in the trans-Saharan gold trade.

questions.q: Robben Island is off the coast of which country?
questions.e: Robben Island is a South African heritage site.

questions.q: What were some historic uses of Robben Island?
questions.e: UNESCO lists these uses across different periods.

questions.q: What does Robben Island’s heritage symbolize?
o: The start of the Swahili language
questions.e: UNESCO links the site to this symbolic history.

questions.q: What type of prison building is prominent on Robben Island?
o: A maximum-security prison for political prisoners
questions.e: UNESCO identifies the maximum-security political prison.

questions.q: Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape is in which country?
questions.e: UNESCO identifies Mapungubwe as a South African site.

questions.q: Which two rivers meet at the Mapungubwe landscape?
questions.e: UNESCO locates it at the Limpopo–Shashe confluence.

questions.q: Mapungubwe is described as an early kingdom in which region?
questions.e: UNESCO calls it the first indigenous kingdom in Southern Africa.

questions.q: Which valuable resources supported Mapungubwe’s trade?
questions.e: UNESCO says its hinterland supplied gold and ivory.

questions.q: Which climate change contributed to Mapungubwe’s decline?
o: A change in monsoon winds in Asia
questions.e: UNESCO connects the kingdom’s decline to drier conditions.

questions.q: Which historic settlement is near the borders of South Africa, Zimbabwe and Botswana?
questions.e: UNESCO places Mapungubwe where those three countries meet.

questions.q: Which kind of town is Stone Town described as?
questions.e: UNESCO describes this settlement as a Swahili trading town.

questions.q: What feature is found on some Stone Town buildings?
questions.e: UNESCO describes elaborately carved doors.

questions.q: Which country is home to the Great Zimbabwe National Monument?
questions.e: UNESCO locates the monument in Zimbabwe.

questions.q: Which people built the civilization represented at Great Zimbabwe?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Great Zimbabwe as a testimony to Shona civilization.

questions.q: Between which centuries did the Shona civilization at Great Zimbabwe flourish?
questions.e: UNESCO dates this civilization from the 11th to the 15th century.

questions.q: What was Great Zimbabwe during the Middle Ages?
questions.e: UNESCO describes it as an important trading centre.

questions.q: Lalibela’s rock-hewn churches are in which country?
questions.e: Lalibela is in the heart of Ethiopia.

questions.q: How many medieval monolithic churches are at Lalibela?
questions.e: UNESCO identifies eleven churches carved from rock.

questions.q: What makes Lalibela’s churches especially distinctive?
questions.e: The churches were carved directly out of rock.

questions.q: Lalibela is still an important place for what?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Lalibela as a place of pilgrimage and devotion.

questions.q: Aksum is an ancient archaeological site in which country?
questions.e: Aksum is in northern Ethiopia.

questions.q: Which monuments are among the ruins at Aksum?
questions.e: UNESCO lists obelisks and giant stelae among its monuments.

questions.q: The ancient Kingdom of Aksum controlled trade connected to which sea?
questions.e: Aksumite fleets controlled trade through the Red Sea.

questions.q: Which historic port is associated with Aksum’s maritime trade?
questions.e: UNESCO names Adulis as the port connected to Aksumite trade.

questions.q: Fort Jesus is in which Kenyan coastal city?
questions.e: Fort Jesus stands in Mombasa.

questions.q: Who built Fort Jesus at the end of the 16th century?
questions.e: UNESCO says the Portuguese built the fort in 1593–1596.

questions.q: What was the main purpose of Fort Jesus when it was built?
questions.e: It was built to protect the port of Mombasa.

questions.q: On what kind of natural feature was Fort Jesus built?
questions.e: UNESCO places the fort on a spur of coral rock.

questions.q: Which architect designed Fort Jesus?
questions.e: UNESCO attributes its design to Giovanni Battista Cairati.

questions.q: Which type of architecture is Fort Jesus an example of?
questions.e: UNESCO calls it an outstanding example of 16th-century Portuguese fortification.

questions.q: Which groups’ cultural influences are visible in Fort Jesus’s history?
o: African, Arab, Turkish, Persian and European
questions.e: UNESCO describes exchanges among these peoples around the port.

questions.q: Which city was the powerful ancient Kingdom of Aksum’s heart?
questions.e: The ruins of Aksum mark the heart of the ancient kingdom.

questions.q: Lalibela is described as a ‘New Jerusalem’ from which century?
questions.e: UNESCO describes the churches as a 13th-century ‘New Jerusalem’.

questions.q: The Great Zimbabwe site covers nearly how much land?
questions.e: UNESCO gives an area of nearly 80 hectares.

questions.q: What kind of cultural landscape surrounds Lalibela’s churches?
o: A mountainous region near a traditional village
questions.e: UNESCO places the churches in a mountain region near a traditional village.

questions.q: Which building tradition is represented by the monumental ruins of Great Zimbabwe?
questions.e: The monument is a testimony to Shona civilization.
